notes: Go HTTP service with a map cache. Ground truth = the 13 findings of Claude Sonnet 5 in plain chat (baseline 2026-08-27, origin 'sonnet5-chat') + 5 real defects nobody reported, found while re-analysing the baseline (origin 'review-2026-09'). The first 13 keep ids G1..G13 so old numbers stay comparable (recall13).

findings.title: Unsynchronized map write in a goroutine
findings.detail: `go func(){ cache[id] = name }()` writes the shared map without cacheMu; concurrent writes crash the whole process with `fatal error: concurrent map writes` (not recoverable). The goroutine is also pointless.

findings.title: RLock used for a map write
findings.detail: `cacheMu.RLock(); cache[id] = name` — a read lock admits several writers at once, so concurrent requests write the map in parallel. Must be Lock().

findings.title: nil resp after an ignored Do error
findings.detail: `resp, _ := httpCli.Do(req)` — on a network error resp is nil and `defer resp.Body.Close()` panics with a nil pointer dereference.

findings.title: All errors swallowed; FetchUser always returns nil error
findings.detail: NewRequest/Do/ReadAll/Unmarshal errors are discarded, so FetchUser's error return is a lie: failures become an empty name that gets cached and served.

findings.title: Data race on the requests counter
findings.detail: `requests++` from concurrent handlers without atomic/mutex loses increments (and the var is unused).

findings.title: panic(err) in an HTTP handler
findings.detail: A fetch failure panics instead of returning an HTTP error: the client gets an aborted connection, logs get a stack trace, no control over the response.

findings.title: 500 for a missing parameter
findings.detail: Missing `id` is a client error → 400 Bad Request, not 500.

findings.title: Upstream status code not checked
findings.detail: A 404/500 from the upstream API is parsed as a User with empty fields and an empty name is cached as a valid answer.

findings.title: Byte-based truncation breaks UTF-8
findings.detail: `name[:10]` slices bytes; a multibyte name (Cyrillic, emoji) is cut mid-rune into an invalid string. Truncate by runes.

findings.title: HTTP client without a timeout
findings.detail: `&http.Client{}` has no Timeout: a hanging upstream blocks the handler goroutine forever.

findings.title: Server without read/write timeouts
findings.detail: `http.ListenAndServe` with no ReadHeaderTimeout/ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout is open to slowloris / slow clients.

findings.title: Unbounded cache
findings.detail: The map cache has no size limit or TTL — memory grows with every unique id.

findings.title: User input concatenated into the upstream URL
findings.detail: `baseURL+"/users/"+id` without escaping: `id` like `../admin` or `1?x=` rewrites the upstream path/query. Use url.PathEscape / url.JoinPath.

findings.title: ListenAndServe error ignored
findings.detail: If the port is taken, ListenAndServe returns an error that is dropped and main exits right after logging 'starting'. Wrap in log.Fatal.

findings.title: Outgoing request not bound to the request context
findings.detail: http.NewRequest instead of NewRequestWithContext(r.Context(), …): a disconnected client does not cancel the upstream call.

findings.title: Unbounded response body read
findings.detail: ReadAll without io.LimitReader: a huge upstream response is read fully into memory.

findings.title: Cache stampede on a miss
findings.detail: Concurrent misses for the same id all call FetchUser; singleflight would collapse them into one upstream call.
